messages.subject: When I can set outputOptions?
parts:
I have some outputs that I want to use outputOptions() on so I can set the priority as they all depend on a single input. However, when the app. loads up they are in a modal which is hidden by default. I put statements such as outputOptions(ouput, "myTextOutput", priority=2)  into my server.r, but I get an error message:

Error in .getReactiveEnvironment()$currentContext() : 
  Operation not allowed without an active reactive context. (You tried to do something that can only be done from inside a reactive expression or observer.)


I think the issue is that the output is hidden from the start, so the observer which holds the output (e..g the renderText() ) does not fire. Is there any way to handle this situation?

messages.subject: Re: When I can set outputOptions?
parts:
Joe,
 Yes, I can eliminate the error by commenting the outputOptions out and  reproduce by restoring the outputOptions. If it is of any help, I have using shiny-leaflet to add a GeoJson layer (map$addGeoJSON), and also I am adding a Legend in a modal window. I am doing this on shinyApps. The problem is that the legend will not display, and I think the issue is that the GeoJson layer takes so long it messes up the Legend outputs. I am hoping to fix this by first producing the Legend and then doing addGeoJSON.


However,  if you know of a way I can tell when the map$addGeoJSON is done so I can use that as a trigger for the legends, that would be great.

Thanks
John Paul

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: When I can set outputOptions?
parts:
I'm not sure why addGeoJSON taking a long time would mess up the legend. But putting the legend in a modal might make it so that Shiny doesn't even know the legend is there. How exactly is your modal implemented? Can you try defining your modal as usual and add

outputOptions(ouput, "myTextOutput", suspendWhenHidden=FALSE)

right below that?
